run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Make `Field.Control` sync controlled `value` changes into field state (dirty, filled, validity) the same way every sibling control already does via `useValueChanged`, fixing a stuck `data-dirty` for non-string values, stale state after programmatic changes, an ignored `details.cancel()`, and a rejected or rewritten controlled value leaking into field state.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue; issue alignment unavailable. Judged against the pull-request title and body (recorded as `spec-pr5460`, supplied inline), which fully accounts for the code change; every stated claim is met by the diff and its added tests.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed for both changed files; `useValueChanged`, `useRegisterFieldControl`, `useFieldControlRegistration`, `useFieldValidation`, `useStableCallback`, and `createChangeEventDetails` read for the surrounding contract. Focused test `FieldControl.test.tsx` run once at the pinned head in jsdom: 26 passed, 1 skipped (browser-only SSR case, unaffected by this diff). One concurrency safety premise, about stale-async-validator supersession, was verified: holds.

observations.fact: No test in this diff exercises a controlled array `value`, though the PR body claims the fix also resolves array-value dirty tracking.
observations.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:34's `serializedValue = value == null ? undefined : String(value)` is applied uniformly regardless of value type, and the same mechanism is exercised only for a numeric `value` by FieldControl.test.tsx's "clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value".

requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:105-114 wires `useValueChanged(serializedValue, ...)` so controlled prop changes reach dirty/filled/validity like every sibling control; FieldControl.test.tsx's added tests pass (26/27, 1 browser-only skip) at 14d39e5d1.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/body/"data-dirty stayed set even after the user returned the field to its initial value"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:34 serializes `value` via `String(value)` before registering it, and useFieldControlRegistration.ts:97 captures that same serialized value as the baseline, so `serializedValue !== (validityData.initialValue ?? '')` compares like types; FieldControl.test.tsx's "clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value" passes. The array-value half of this claim is not independently tested (see observation).

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/body/"a resolved error stayed visible and a pending async validator for the old value could still publish"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:105-114 fires clearErrors/setDirty/setFilled/validation.change from the resolved controlled value; FieldControl.test.tsx's "syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically" passes. Verified safety premise `premise-1` (holds): useFieldValidation.ts's monotonic `validationCommitIdRef` still supersedes a stale in-flight async `validate()` after this change.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/body/"details.cancel() in onValueChange now stops the internal handling"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:141 adds `&& !details.isCanceled` to the clearErrors/validation.change guard; FieldControl.test.tsx's "does not validate when the change is canceled" passes.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/body/"A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:135-137 returns from `onChange` before any state update once `isControlled` is true, so a value the parent does not echo back through `value` never reaches setDirty/setFilled/validation.change.

The per-validation-mode keystroke render-count table is a jsdom benchmark narrative; only the general "renders once per keystroke once settled" claim is covered by the added test (which passed), not the exact onSubmit-vs-onChange counts in the table.

tasks.premise: When FieldControl.tsx's useValueChanged effect calls validation.change(serializedValue) for a newer controlled value, useFieldValidation.ts's commit()'s monotonic validationCommitIdRef supersession still discards the result of any still-pending async validate() call started for a stale (older or rejected) value, so a stale async validator can never publish its result over the field's current validity state after this change.
tasks.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:105-114 (useValueChanged→validation.change on prop change); useFieldValidation.ts:117-119,262-271,316-328 (monotonic validationCommitIdRef supersedes a stale async validate() across both the debounced-timeout and immediate commit paths, and useTimeout.start clears any pending timeout first); useValueChanged.ts:10-16 (fires only on an actual value change). Verifier ruling: holds.
